summary: A clump of instanced reed blades on a faceted tussock, with seed heads carried on the blade tips and an animate(dt) that bends every blade about its own base.
objective: At one metre the clump reads as a fan of blades of different heights over a tussock, then each blade curving its own way with seed heads, then tapered tips and hue jitter.
example_prompts: Line the pond edge with reeds that move in the wind.
I need grass I can instance across a bank without forty draw calls.
not_for: Any claim about a plant species, its habitat or its growth.
A wind field: the sway is a per-blade phase, not a simulated force.

silhouette: forty blades whose heights vary from half to 1.1 times the height parameter
a low faceted tussock the blades grow out of
the clump fanning out rather than standing as a bundle
medium: every blade swept along its own azimuth, so no two curve the same way
two blade curvatures in the clump, one gentle and one strongly hooked
about a third of the blades carrying an elongated seed head at the tip
fine: blades tapering from 14 mm at the sheath to 3 mm at the tip
the seed head carried in the same geometry space as the blade, so it can never drift off its stem
per-blade hue jitter of 8 percent across the whole clump

principles: A blade that grows straight up reads as a spike. The quadratic sweep is what makes a clump read as a plant.
The seed head is placed in the blade geometry, not in a second placement list, so one instance transform carries both and they can never separate.
Wind is per-blade phase and per-blade gust strength: a clump that bends as one object reads as a rubber prop.
implementation: Call create({ count, seed, spread, height, blade }); the clump is centred on the origin with the ground plane at y = 0.
animate(dt, strength) - also exported as sway(dt) - recomposes every instance matrix and returns true when it moved; it returns false for dt <= 0.
instancing gives { geometry, material, hueJitter } for a unit blade standing on y = 0 with its tip at y = 1, so an instance scale is the blade height in metres.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible.
count 90 produces more than three times the triangles of count 12 at the same seed.
animate(0) returns false, animate(0.4) returns true and changes the instance matrices.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here measures a real reed, sedge or grass.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at the default count of forty; a count of ninety costs about 4300 triangles and breaks the 2500 ceiling. The budget is per default count.
Blades are three-sided tapered prisms, not cards: they read from every angle but they cannot show a flat leaf face.
animate() rewrites every instance matrix on the CPU each call, so a bank of many clumps should share one clump and animate it once rather than call each.

Palette values are the colours that render: kit-core scatterInstances runs its InstancedMesh on a white-based clone of the material and writes the absolute jittered colour per instance, so an unjittered instance lands on exactly the hex the parameter names.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Raise the height and drop the count for bulrushes, or shrink both and re-colour for a tussock of meadow grass.

defaults.rationale: 1.25 m puts the tallest blades at waist height on a 1.7 m figure, the height at which reeds read as water margin rather than as lawn.
